s1.syndrome_frame: Acute chest pain with electrocardiographic changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers
salient_findings: ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and PR-segment depression
Elevated high-sensitivity troponin I and brain-type natriuretic peptide
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 60s
History of hypertension
No history of acute febrile illness
No family history of sudden cardiac death
Tachycardic with a pulse of 120 beats/min
Normal blood pressure
White blood cell count of 14,300/µL
Serum calcium within normal limits
High-sensitivity troponin I of 1.15 ng/mL
Brain-type natriuretic peptide of 1060.30 pg/mL
ECG showed sinus tachycardia and ST-segment elevation in multiple leads
Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries
Left ventriculography confirmed systolic apical ballooning
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT revealed a left-adrenal heterogeneous mass

shortlist.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Apical ballooning on left ventriculography and normal coronary arteries

shortlist.label: Pheochromocytoma
shortlist.why_kept: Left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on CT and elevated troponin

shortlist.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: ECG changes and elevated cardiac biomarkers without coronary artery disease

shortlist.label: Adrenal carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Left-adrenal heterogeneous mass on CT and potential for catecholamine-induced cardiomyopathy

shortlist.label: Apical ballooning syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: ECG changes and apical ballooning on left ventriculography, similar to Takotsubo cardiomyopathy

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with sudden-onset chest pain, tachycardia, and elevated troponin levels, combined with the ECG findings and the confirmation of systolic apical ballooning on left ventriculography, is highly suggestive of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. The presence of a left-adrenal heterogeneous mass could be an incidental finding or a contributing stressor.

rejected.label: Pheochromocytoma
rejected.why: While the adrenal mass could suggest pheochromocytoma, the normal blood pressure and lack of other specific symptoms make this less likely.

rejected.label: Stress cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: This is essentially synonymous with Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, and the latter term is more commonly used to describe this condition.

rejected.label: Adrenal carcinoma
rejected.why: The presence of an adrenal mass does not directly explain the cardiac findings, and there is no other evidence to suggest adrenal carcinoma as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Apical ballooning syndrome
rejected.why: This is another term for Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, and the latter is a more comprehensive description of the condition.
